videos.title: Responsive Web Design
videos.notes:
Responsive Web Design (RWD) makes web pages look good on all devices — desktops, tablets, and phones. Uses the HTML <meta> viewport tag to control layout scaling on different screen sizes. Fluid grids use relative units (%, vw) instead of fixed pixels so layouts resize automatically. Flexible images and media scale within their containers to avoid overflow. CSS media queries apply different styles based on device width, height, or orientation.

Code Example:

<!-- In <head> section -->
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">

/* Fluid container */
.container {
 width: 100%;
 max-width: 1200px;
 margin: 0 auto;
}

videos.title: Media Queries
videos.notes:
Media queries apply CSS rules only when certain device conditions are met (width, height, orientation). Syntax: @media only screen and (max-width: 600px) { ... } Breakpoints are the screen widths where the layout changes (e.g., 600px, 768px, 1024px). Mobile-first design writes default styles for small screens, then uses min-width queries to scale up.

Code Example:

/* Mobile first — default */
.col { width: 100%; }
/* Tablet: 601px+ */
@media (min-width: 601px) {
 .col { width: 50%; }
}
/* Desktop: 993px+ */
@media (min-width: 993px) {
 .col { width: 25%; }
}

videos.title: Flexbox
videos.notes:
Flexbox (Flexible Box Layout) is a 1D layout model for arranging items in a row or column. Set display: flex on a parent container to make its children flex items. justify-content controls horizontal alignment: flex-start, center, space-between, space-around. align-items controls vertical alignment: stretch, center, flex-start, flex-end. flex-wrap: wrap allows items to wrap onto the next line when there isn't enough space.

Code Example:

.flex-container {
 display: flex;
 flex-direction: row;
 flex-wrap: wrap;
 justify-content: space-between;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 16px;
}
.flex-item {
 flex: 1;
 min-width: 200px;
}

videos.title: CSS Transforms
videos.notes:
The transform property applies 2D or 3D visual transformations to an element without affecting document flow. translate(x, y) moves an element horizontally and/or vertically. rotate(deg) rotates an element. scale(x, y) resizes an element. skew(x, y) tilts an element. Multiple transforms can be chained in a single property. transform-origin changes the pivot point.

Code Example:

/* 2D Transforms */
.move { transform: translate(50px, 20px); }
.spin { transform: rotate(45deg); }
.grow { transform: scale(1.5); }
.tilt { transform: skewX(20deg); }
/* Combined */
.combo { transform: rotate(30deg) scale(0.8); }

videos.title: CSS Transitions
videos.notes:
CSS transitions smoothly animate a property change from one value to another over a set duration. transition-property specifies which CSS property to animate. transition-duration sets how long the transition takes. transition-timing-function controls the speed curve. transition-delay adds a pause before the transition starts. Use 'all' to transition every animatable property.

Code Example:

.btn {
 background: #7B5EA7;
 color: white;
 padding: 10px 24px;
 transition: background 0.3s ease, transform 0.3s ease;
}
.btn:hover {
 background: #CC44AA;
 transform: scale(1.05);
}

videos.title: CSS Animations
videos.notes:
CSS animations allow elements to gradually change style using @keyframes and the animation property. @keyframes defines the animation steps: from/to or percentage-based. animation-name links an element to a @keyframes rule. animation-duration sets how long one cycle takes. animation-fill-mode: forwards keeps the end-state style after the animation completes.

Code Example:

@keyframes slideIn {
 from { transform: translateX(-100%); opacity: 0; }
 to { transform: translateX(0); opacity: 1; }
}
.box {
 animation: slideIn 0.6s ease-out forwards;
}
